tutorial._note: 打字教程教学句池：分步课程 / 教学 / 导师
sentences: Lesson one: find the home row and rest eight fingers gently on the keys.
Lesson two: press each key with the nearest finger, then return home.
Lesson three: type the letters a s d f and j k l without looking down.
Lesson four: add the space bar with your thumb between every word.
Lesson five: stretch up to the number row and always come back home.
Lesson six: practice the shift key with the pinky of the opposite hand.
Lesson seven: drill the punctuation keys until they feel like letters.
Lesson eight: copy a short paragraph and count your errors out loud.
Lesson nine: type the same paragraph again and beat your error count.
Lesson ten: set a two minute timer and type at a pace you can hold.
A good tutorial explains why a finger owns a key, not just which one.
Begin each session with a slow warmup before chasing any speed.
Learning the map of the keyboard is the lesson that pays for itself daily.
Tutorials work when you repeat the dull drills until they stop feeling dull.
Read the instructions once, then let your hands do the learning.
A lesson is only finished when your fingers can repeat it alone.
Keep tutorial sessions short so your hands stay fresh for each drill.
Review the weakest keys at the end of every tutorial session.
The best learners type a new drill until it is boring, then once more.
Progress in a tutorial is measured by clean lines, not rushing minutes.
Each lesson is a small brick; daily practice builds the wall.
A tutorial that mixes review and new keys keeps both memory and interest.
When a lesson feels easy, that is the moment to lengthen the passage.

The first drill is always the hardest, and it is always the most important.

Type each example exactly as written; accuracy is the lesson, not speed.
When the tutorial feels too easy, add one minute instead of rushing it.

Every lesson starts with the home row and ends with two steady hands.
A tutorial is a map; daily practice is the journey across it.

Trust the lesson sequence; skipping ahead is how beginners stall.
Type each tutorial line three times: once for accuracy, once for rhythm, once for speed.

sentences: A good typing tutor watches the keys so your eyes do not have to.

Open the tutor, pick a drill, and let the timer do the teaching.

The tutor does not care about yesterday; it only reads the line in front of you.
Start a drill at half speed and let the tutor confirm your accuracy before you rush.
